Experience

Apr 2026 —

Interaction UX Design for Public Education

Justus-von-Liebig Grundschule · Berlin, Germany · On-site

This project is part of Expanded Classroom, a series of digital projects for public schools in Berlin.

Designing and developing an interactive, collective artifact (6m long) in a public school in Berlin. This artifact operates as a social design system grounded in a reverse-technology approach: digital paradigms such as personalized interfaces are translated into a physical environment, democratizing access to participation and experience.

Through a modular system, each student actively contributes to the construction of the artifact, shifting away from individual-use logic toward a collective, tangible system that extends beyond the constraints of digital devices. The project engages six educational levels, enabling intergenerational co-creation.

The artifact simultaneously functions as a physical data visualization representing the school's student body. It integrates accessibility principles through the use of Braille to encode names, reducing the risk of bullying while promoting inclusive communication. Mathematical concepts such as quantity and proportion are embedded within the system.

Social Design · Democracy · Accessibility · Physical Computing

2025-2026

Lead UI/UX & Brand Designer

Puquelinhue / Cía. Ltda.

I worked freelance on the rebranding and website redesign of the Puquelinhue Ecological Reserve, a park located on Chiloé Island that promotes sustainable ecotourism and is undergoing a process of reinvention. This project progresses in stages that I resume between other professional assignments. As part of the collaboration, I conduct UX research with visitors and local stakeholders through surveys and interviews, applying Design Thinking to co-create inclusive and culturally relevant solutions. I also provide strategic brand consulting and develop a cohesive visual identity, while working closely with the team to define the voice and narrative that best reflect the park's values of native forest conservation, Chiloé's cultural heritage, and community participation. My work focuses on improving the visitor experience and strengthening the communication of the park's mission through accessible, community-centered design with social impact, supporting its transition toward a model of sustainable and participatory tourism.

May 2025 — Jul 2025

UX & Social Design / Community Branding

Justus-von-Liebig Grundschule · Berlin, Germany · Hybrid

This project was carried out as part of the 30th anniversary celebration of the school, with the initial goal of redesigning the logo, which until then had not been accessible or scalable, and later to encourage community participation around a shared identity.

I redesigned the primary school's logo and developed its application across stationery and textiles. To achieve this, I implemented a methodology of active participation in the Lehrerversammlung, Elternversammlung, and Schülerversammlung, where I presented and justified my design decisions in German. Together, we defined elements such as typography and colors through open hand-raise voting. This process allowed the school community to disassociate from external identities and identify more closely with the school itself and its values.

The student body participated particularly actively, strengthening their sense of belonging by deciding to include the youngest classes (first and second grade) in the decision-making process. I also translated the digital design into print formats, creating an adaptable logo suitable for use on textiles through one-color screen printing on T-shirts for students and teachers, ensuring consistency between digital (Webpage) and physical media.

2023 · 2024

UI/UX Product Designer

Plunet.com / SaaS

Redesign of the Test System Manager · a centralized tool to manage BM instances, deploy data snapshots, and monitor services. Structured around weekly CoP meetings, dark-mode interface using the PlunetBoard design system.

Figma · Mural · Jira · Confluence

Context

The Test System Manager (TSM) originated from the need to streamline how internal teams managed test environments. Until then, system administrators and dev teams relied on fragmented interfaces to configure instances, deploy data snapshots, and monitor diagnostics. The previous tool lacked usability, was hard to scale, and failed to surface critical functionality efficiently — especially for non-expert users.

Goal

Redesign the TSM control panel as a centralized, intuitive tool to manage BusinessManager (BM) instances, streamline configurations, deploy data snapshots, and monitor services — while ensuring extensibility for future features. Improve usability, reduce time spent on repetitive admin tasks, and support both technical and non-technical users.

Process

An iterative, collaborative redesign structured around weekly Community of Practice meetings. Key pain points emerged from sessions with developers, QA engineers, and system administrators — revealing the need for better log visibility, faster snapshot deployment, and a clearer overview of BM instances.

The information architecture was restructured to reflect users' mental models, with a dark-mode interface built on the PlunetBoard design system — reusing its component library to ensure consistency and optimize resources. Interactive Figma prototypes validated critical flows like system configuration, service control, and log viewing.

Outcome

Successfully adopted by development and testing teams as the primary tool for managing test systems. Feedback highlighted faster task completion, clearer visibility of critical information, and a smoother workflow. The modular design also enabled rapid incorporation of new features post-launch.

2023 · 2024

UI product designer for "PlunetBoard"

Plunet.com / SaaS

I worked on the design system components, ensuring consistent alignment of interface resources across the product area. I analyzed the legacy software design and evaluated the company's website to integrate visual coherence between both platforms, contributing to a unified brand identity.

Based on these analyses, I designed from scratch the visual identity of PlunetBoard, Plunet's new data visualization dashboard. This included defining the navigation structure, designing content layouts, creating widgets, and implementing filters to enable users to effectively visualize information. I participated in the MVP, Beta, and Delta phases, culminating in the completion of three releases during the initial phase of corporate image update.

Context

The project emerged in response to a recurring internal need: the lack of a clear, centralized tool to visualize the status of tasks, requests, and key system metrics. Until then, users were juggling multiple tools, spreadsheets, and communication channels · making it difficult to prioritize, monitor progress, or detect bottlenecks.

Team

4 Product Owners · 4 Frontend Engineers · 4 QA Engineers · Backend team

Tools: Figma · Adobe Suite · Jira · Confluence · Angular Material · Mural

Phase 01

Alpha · MVP

4 months

Created the main dashboard functionality from scratch, including basic widgets: Pending Requests, Overdue Orders, and Today's Highlights. Simple list filtering and scrollable/expandable lists.

Phase 02

Beta · Filters & Semantics

4 months

Added customer search filters, semantic color KPI indicators (green/yellow/red), and new widgets: My Open Items, My Marked Tasks, and 7-Day Request History.

Phase 03

Delta · Personalisation

5 months

Advanced customizable filters, resizable and rearrangeable columns, alphabetical sorting. Users can now build their own view.

Outcome

92SUS Score / A+
75%Team adoption
−25%Task prioritization time
80%KPI adoption after Beta

2022

UI/UX Designer

Green-Coding.io / SaaS

I worked as part of a team of three designers, with the challenge of rethinking the website’s architecture and exploring new visual and interactive proposals. My role focused on defining the user flow and the MVP, where I proposed and developed a console-like interface inspired by the minimalist aesthetics of 1990s terminals as a visual resource that reinforced the idea of simplicity and accessibility.

This approach was complemented by the choice of a high-contrast black-and-white scheme, which not only broke away from the widespread use of green in the “green tech” sector —where the absence of color functioned as a visual metaphor for “minimal use of resources”— but also positioned the website as “the black-and-white page that is easy to navigate.”

Figma · Google Forms · GitHub

Context

Green Coding is a platform that measures energy consumption and CO₂ emissions from software and websites. The goal was to redesign the homepage, add functionalities like project comparison, and create a "Showcases" section · all while prioritizing clarity in the presentation of complex data.

Team & Tools

Role: UI/UX Designer

Figma · Google Forms · GitHub

Phase 01

Research

Stakeholder interviews and user surveys revealed that 96% of users were interested in reducing their digital footprint but unsure how. In-depth exploration of digital energy consumption and sustainable design limitations informed the direction.

Phase 02

Definition

Reorganized the information architecture to promote ethical and ecological navigation. Defined the primary User Persona: Joao, a developer concerned about his environmental impact who needed a tool that was clear, fast, and actionable without greenwashing aesthetics.

Phase 03

Ideation & Design

Black and white palette · chosen for clarity, accessibility, and to stand apart from the clichéd green palette common in eco-design. Visual metaphor inspired by a developer console: clear hierarchy, low cognitive load, and a scalable structure that communicates precision rather than decoration.

Result

A functional, static, minimalist, and accessible MVP that allows users to:

CO₂Measure emissions from any website or software
↔Compare projects visually and simply
96%Users interested in reducing footprint but unsure how

This project represented a turning point, as I faced the challenge of designing for people seeking to plan their vacations. Although at that time I lacked formal knowledge in user-centered UX design, my intuition led me to investigate the needs of visitors, observe their motivations, and validate design proposals with them. In an effort to create a clear and coherent experience, I defined key interactions and carried out usability tests with the first wireframes.
